description: Boréale for Nintendo Switch, the Home Assistant integration of the Boréale homebrews: PlayGuard's play time, limits, extra time and statistics, over your own MQTT broker.
f1_text: Today's play time per game and per account, the day's limit and what is left, bedtime, the week: and the controls to change them, with the same checks as on the console.
f2_text: Nothing goes through a cloud: the console and Home Assistant talk over your MQTT broker, on your network. No account to create, nothing sent elsewhere.
f3_text: Triggers, conditions and actions of its own, blueprints ready to import, and Assist: ask how long they played, or give thirty more minutes.
f4_text: Play time per game and per account in Home Assistant's long-term statistics, for charts over months, beyond the fourteen days the console keeps.
features_lede: Each console is a device, found on the broker by itself. Everything PlayGuard publishes becomes sensors, controls and events you can put on a dashboard or in an automation.
features_title: The console's parental controls, as entities

hero_lede: Boréale for Nintendo Switch brings the Boréale homebrews into Home Assistant: today's play time, the limits, extra time in one tap, bedtime and long-term statistics, from PlayGuard, over your own MQTT broker.
hero_title: Your Switch, at home in Home Assistant
install_lede: It needs Home Assistant 2026.10 or later with its MQTT integration, and PlayGuard on the console with its remote link turned on.
legal_lede: What this site learns about you, and who is behind it.

move_text: Installed under its former name? Update it: each console is taken over by itself, with its entities, their history and its statistics. A repair then says what is left to change in your automations.
notice_contact_text: An issue on GitHub; a security flaw, privately on GitHub.
notice_publisher_text: JigSawFr, a non-professional publisher, whose identity is held by the host, as French law (LCEN) allows.
notice_rights_text: The site's and the integration's code is free software under the GPLv3 (its repository); the names Boréale and PlayGuard, and their marks, are reserved. Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo; Home Assistant, of the Open Home Foundation.
privacy_1: This site sets no cookie, and keeps nothing in your browser but the language you choose in its header. It loads nothing from another site: its fonts, images and scripts are served with it.
privacy_2: It counts its visits with Umami Cloud, in the European Union (Frankfurt), without cookie. For each page seen: the page, the page you came from, your browser, system and kind of device, your screen's size, your language and your country. Your IP address is used to tell your country and to tell visits apart, and is not kept with them. The counts are kept six months, used only to know what is read, and never sold or shared. Umami's policy: umami.is/privacy.
privacy_3: Boréale's other sites (boreale.dev and its projects') are counted the same way. GitHub, which serves them, records its visitors' IP addresses for its servers' security (GitHub's privacy statement). The integration itself sends nothing to this site or to anyone else.
privacy_4: For a question about your data, or to have it erased: an issue on GitHub. You may also complain to your data protection authority; in France, the CNIL.
promise_text: Free software under the GPLv3, with no account, no cloud and no advertising. Its code is on GitHub, for anyone to read, check or improve.

step1_text: The button below opens the repository in your HACS (or add https://github.com/JigSawFr/boreale-ha as a custom repository, type Integration), then download it and restart Home Assistant.
step2_text: In PlayGuard, Console › Remote access: the same broker as Home Assistant's, until the status reads Online. Its guide has the details.
step3_text: It shows up in Settings › Devices & services › Discovered: confirm it. Nothing to type.
